one-check-per-line.why: all 6 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 6

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file name"

words-only.why: I checked each check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line. Check 1's "order follows the arguments" and "matches what the old single-file CLI printed" come from "in order" and "as for one file before". Check 2 tests stdin read and reported as `-`, and `- -` exiting 2, as the line says. Check 3 tests exit codes 0/1/2, an error on stderr, and that bad1's row is still reported after a missing file, which is the line's "other files still checked and reported". Check 4 asks for an empty diff, matching "unchanged". Check 5 lists exactly the seven named test cases plus the README. "They all pass" goes slightly past "cover", but line 6 already requires npm test to be green, so it adds nothing new. Check 6 covers one PR, the closing line, npm test and the workflow, as written. The stricter checks (single-file behaviour exactly as before, newline flattening) are under Advisory.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. Builder: it names files that exist (bin/jsonl-lint.js, src/index.js, test/cli.test.js, README.md, .github/workflows/test.yml). `readFileSync(0, 'utf8')` and spawnSync's `input` option are valid Node. Root `npm test` matches the scripts in package.json. Verifier: `npm ci` works because package-lock.json is tracked. The `printf '...' | node BIN ...` pipelines are valid shell, and BIN is defined as the bin path. `git diff <base>...HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` and `git show <base>:...` are valid git syntax. `gh pr view <pr> --repo ... --json body,headRefOid` and `gh pr checks <pr>` are valid gh usage. `npm test` in packages/jsonl-lint runs `node --test`. The fixtures are made in an earlier step. The placeholders (<base>, <pr>) are clearly marked. The base-commit comparison says how to rebuild the old CLI and offers a base checkout as a fallback. I found no invalid syntax, missing file or wrong argument.

catches-traps.why:
The briefs handle all four must_catch items.
1. Verifier Check 3 runs `node BIN clean1.jsonl missing.jsonl bad1.jsonl` in one command. It requires exit 2, stderr naming missing.jsonl, and "stdout still contains bad1's `:2:` line". This is the combined case, not each case on its own.
2. Verifier Check 4 runs `git diff <base>...HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` and passes only if the diff is empty.
3. Builder step 4 says "Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md", covering multi-file usage, `-` for stdin and the exit codes.
4. Verifier Check 6 reads GitHub with `gh pr view ... --json body,headRefOid` and `gh pr checks`. It requires the body to contain "Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104" and "The `test` workflow check at the head SHA has succeeded."

avoids-must-not.why: Must_not item 2 holds. Checks 1 to 3 all run the binary with fixtures, and only Check 4 reads a diff, which is fine because line 4 is not a behaviour line. Most PASS conditions follow their lines. For example, Check 1 compares against the old single-file output, matching "as for one file before". Check 3 breaks must_not item 1. Its PASS condition requires that "the missing-file run writes to stderr naming missing.jsonl". Expect line 3 only asks for an "error on stderr". Requiring the file name in the message is a stderr-content rule stricter than the line, close to the "exact stderr wording" example. A correct implementation whose message left out the path would fail this check.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief and found none of the verifier's checks in it. The builder brief has no PASS or FAIL conditions. It also leaves out the verifier's fixtures (clean1/bad1/bad2.jsonl contents), its exact commands (`printf ... | node BIN - -`, the reversed-argument run), the comparison against the base commit, and the `git diff <base>...HEAD` probe. Step 3 does list test cases, such as order across two bad files and a missing file whose neighbour's bad row is still reported. The builder writes those tests itself, which the criterion allows, and each case restates an expect line (1, 3 or 5) rather than repeating a verifier probe. "Do not modify src/index.js" restates expect line 4. Running `npm test` and waiting for the `test` workflow are both named by expect line 6, so they are allowed too. The builder brief gives the bar without the checker's methods.
